title: Beyond the 956: Alan Jones, 1980 Formula 1 world champion, dies at 80
excerpt: Alan Jones, the 1980 Formula 1 world champion and the last Australian to win the title, has died at 80. His family announced on November 5, 2026, that he died following a short illness, just three days after his 80th birthday.
content:
🌎 BEYOND THE 956

Alan Jones, the 1980 Formula 1 world champion and the last Australian to win the sport's drivers' title, has died at 80.

Jones died on Thursday, November 5, 2026, following a short illness, his family announced in a statement issued through Motorsport Australia. He had celebrated his 80th birthday just three days earlier, on November 2.

"We are extremely saddened to announce the passing of our beloved Alan, who passed away on 5 November following a short illness," his wife, Amanda Butler-Davis, said in the statement.

Born on November 2, 1946, in Melbourne, Australia, Jones was the son of racing driver Stan Jones, winner of the 1959 Australian Grand Prix. He made his Formula 1 debut at the 1975 Spanish Grand Prix and raced in the sport until 1986.

Jones won 12 grands prix across his Formula 1 career, 11 of them with Williams. In 1980, he became Williams' first world champion, winning five races — in Argentina, France, Britain, Canada and the United States — and clinching the drivers' title ahead of Brazilian Nelson Piquet. Williams also won its first constructors' championship that year.

He remains, more than four decades later, only the second Australian to win the Formula 1 world championship, after three-time champion Sir Jack Brabham, and the last Australian to do so. He was also the last local driver to win the Australian Grand Prix, at Calder Park in Melbourne in 1980.

Formula 1 confirmed his death on Thursday, and tributes poured in from across the sport. Motorsport Australia president Alan Fraser said Jones' place in the history of Australian motorsport is assured. Jones is survived by his wife, Amanda, and his children Christian, Amber, Zara, Jack, Camilla and Emma.

Rest in Peace, Alan Jones.

Sources: Formula 1; Sky Sports; Motorsport Australia, via the family's statement; RACER.
